title: How Unitree's Kung Fu Robot Learned to Fight
description:
Unitree's new H2-X robot flips over a car, kicks dents into doors and "guards" a woman from a knife in its launch video (21 Oct 2026), and Unitree labels the footage "Real Footage Throughout No Speed-Up". How does a robot learn moves like that? Robots like it start by copying a person's motion, joint by joint, then practise it as thousands of virtual copies in a simulator, falling over until the move works. Unitree's own public training code (unitree_rl_gym) trains 4,096 simulated robots at once by default, and its controller acts every 0.02 seconds (50 times a second). But the video's own small print says the "approximately 8 hours" of endurance is for standing, and labels the knife scene a "Security Demonstration".

Footage: Unitree Robotics, "Unitree Introducing: H2-X Kung Fu Legend Guardian" (YouTube, 21 Oct 2026), used in short clips under our commentary, slowed with frame interpolation: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Y3zb4o47yqA
The simulator scenes are our own 3D illustration, not Unitree footage.

Sources:
Unitree's training code (Train > Play > Sim2Sim > Sim2Real; num_envs = 4096; sim dt 0.005 s x decimation 4): https://github.com/unitreerobotics/unitree_rl_gym
KungfuBot, how human kung fu motion is retargeted and learned on a Unitree G1 (NeurIPS 2025): https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.12851
H2-X specs and price not yet published (BigGo Finance): https://finance.biggo.com/news/b25f76b1-9b05-4d74-9d7d-f3df2163154c

Narration uses an AI voice. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Unitree.
